reason: Attacked and it holds. Wording: Thorin's dying speech reads “There is more in you of good than you know, child of the kindly West. Some courage and some wisdom, blended in measure. If more of us valued food and cheer and song above hoarded gold, it would be a merrier world. But sad or merry, I must leave it now. Farewell!” The proposed sentence is lifted whole, in order, with its own capital and its own full stop. Two independent witnesses agree word for word: the full chapter text at esl-bits.eu and SparkNotes' Famous Quotes Explained page for The Hobbit, which prints the same sentence and assigns it to chapter 18. The claim that the line belongs only to the 1977 Rankin and Bass adaptation is false and the chapter text kills it. Locator: The Hobbit has nineteen chapters and chapter XVIII is The Return Journey, which is the chapter that holds Thorin's death; correct. Attribution and speaker: Thorin Oakenshield, named in the source, and the misattribution list's Tolkien trap (Not all who wander are lost) is a different line and not in play. Scope: a novel first published 1937, imaginative literature, no scripture, no film, no lyric, no oratory, nothing post-1999. Publishable: a dying man's speech but no description of the wound or the dying; nothing here needs a warning. Form: the source line leads with the author's name, has no dash, uses no straight double quote, and runs 115 characters against the 140 cap; the speaker parenthesis sits after the edition parenthesis, which is the pattern the February carry-in Ian Fleming, Casino Royale, chapter 20, The Nature of Evil (Jonathan Cape, 1953) (Rene Mathis) already set. Tag Fiction is the form of the work. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, Tolkien banned false, yearCount 2 in months 5 and 7, atCap false. TWO CAUTIONS FOR THE EDITOR, neither of them a refutation. First, the witness is not a 1937 Allen and Unwin scan but modern full text transcriptions; Thorin's speech was not touched by the 1951 or 1966 revisions, which reworked chapter 5, so the risk is small, but the edition named in the source is not the edition anybody read. Second and more serious, this is the LAST Tolkien slot in the year and it is already spoken for. Tolkien stands at 2, and the carry list holds three Tolkien lines all marked fitMonth 9: 03-cfl-07 (small hands do them because they must), whose own note says in terms that Tolkien's small hands is already held for September, plus 06-cfl-06 (letter 213) and 02-cfl-05 (the wide world is all about you). Rule 8 forbids a person twice in a month and caps the year at three, so at most one Tolkien can land in September and the verified carry-in has prior claim. If the editor takes this Hobbit line, the three carried Tolkiens are dead for the year, not merely for the month.
